title: A maritime migration surge redirected Coast Guard capacity and changed the balance among missions
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107440 review of Coast Guard maritime migrant and drug interdiction missions and DHS Operation Vigilant Sentry
geography: Caribbean Sea, Florida Straits, Southeast District, and other U.S. Coast Guard districts; fiscal years 2015–2024 with surge operation beginning August 2022

observations.period: Fiscal years 2021–2024; maritime migration surge and Coast Guard mission resources

denominator.unit: Coast Guard statutory missions considered in operational-hour and expense comparisons

migrant_operational_hours_change.unit: percent increase in vessel and aircraft operational hours for migrant interdiction from FY2021 to FY2023

drug_operational_hours_change.unit: percent decrease in vessel and aircraft operational hours for drug interdiction from FY2021 to FY2023

migrant_flow_change.unit: percent increase in known annual maritime migrant flow from the FY2015–2021 average to approximately 34,000 in each of FY2022 and FY2023

migrant_interdiction_2022_2023.unit: percent of known maritime migrant flow interdicted by the Coast Guard in both FY2022 and FY2023, approximately 12,500 of 34,000

surge_cutters.unit: cutters deployed to Operation Vigilant Sentry in the Southeast District from August 2022 through September 2024; 38 redirected from other missions and 29 mixed-use

observations.method: GAO analyzed Coast Guard operational-hour, expense, drug-interdiction, and migrant-interdiction data; reviewed mission documents; and interviewed headquarters, field, and partner-agency officials. GAO assessed the main data as sufficiently reliable for the stated measures.
observations.uncertainty: Operational hours and interdiction shares show resource allocation and recorded outcomes, not total migration, deterrence, migrant safety after interception, drug availability, or causal effects of any single policy.
observations.subgroup: Coast Guard drug and migrant interdiction missions, Operation Vigilant Sentry, Southeast District assets, other statutory missions, and foreign or federal partner agencies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Migrant interdiction was described as partly life-saving and may reasonably receive higher priority; lower drug or other mission activity can reflect deliberate prioritization, asset readiness, partner substitution, or changing flows rather than simple institutional failure.

observations.period: Fiscal years 2021–2024; partner substitution and performance measurement

denominator.unit: Operation Vigilant Sentry and Coast Guard/DHS maritime migrant-interdiction coordination route

jiatf_cutter_support.value: 50% of requested cutter support in FY2023 versus 96% in FY2021
jiatf_cutter_support.unit: Coast Guard contribution to JIATF-South requests

partner_share_drug_interdictions.unit: share of drug interdictions attributed to partner nations in JIATF-South data

drug_mass_seized.value: approximately 143,000 kilograms in FY2021 versus 110,000 kilograms in FY2023
drug_mass_seized.unit: drugs seized by the Coast Guard

lessons_learned.value: the task force generally followed 7 of 8 leading collaboration practices but did not fully share lessons learned

observations.method: GAO compared Coast Guard and JIATF-South operational and performance records and assessed DHS task-force documentation and interviews against prior collaboration practices.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison does not establish that Coast Guard resource redirection alone caused drug-seizure changes; partner contributions, route changes, asset readiness, enforcement by other agencies, and measurement definitions also matter.
observations.subgroup: Coast Guard, JIATF-South, United Kingdom and Netherlands partner forces, DHS agencies, and Operation Vigilant Sentry participants.
observations.counterinterpretation: Increased partner participation may represent successful burden sharing rather than loss of U.S. influence; the task force's incomplete lessons-sharing process does not mean coordination was absent.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies maritime-flow, resource-tradeoff, Operation Vigilant Sentry, partner-substitution, performance, and collaboration findings.

boundary: This record establishes a named maritime-interdiction operation and a resource-tradeoff route across Coast Guard missions. It does not establish deterrence, migrant safety or later status, total drug supply, criminal adaptation, public legitimacy, or a causal effect of one policy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO accessible HTML report retrieved and hashed; underlying Coast Guard case files, migrant records, partner logs, and classified operational materials not retained
